content:
The [Meta Tag Generator](/meta-tag-generator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Generate the meta tags for a page — title, description, Open Graph and Twitter Card. Enter your page title and meta description and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Generate the meta tags for a web page: the title, description, canonical link and the Open Graph and Twitter Card tags that control how the page looks when it is shared. Fill in the form and copy the ready-to-paste HTML into your page's <head>. The generator escapes everything properly, fills Open Graph fields from the title and description when you leave them blank, and only includes Twitter Card tags when you choose a card type. To check tags that already exist on a live page, use the Meta Tag Analyzer instead.

## How to use the Meta Tag Generator

Start by typing or pasting your page title, then typing or pasting your meta description. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause.

1. Fill in the title, description and any other fields you need.
2. Open Graph fields copy from the title and description when left blank.
3. Copy the generated HTML and paste it into your page's <head>.

## How it works

The [Meta Tag Generator](/meta-tag-generator) works straight from the values you enter: change an input and the result updates immediately, with no page reload and no waiting. Everything happens in your browser, so your entries never leave your device. Try it with a few different values and you will quickly get a feel for how the inputs move the result.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. A page titled “CalcHub — Free Online Calculators” with the description “Free online calculators for finance, health, maths and more.” generates a <title>, a meta description, og:title, og:description, og:type and a twitter:card — ready to paste into the page head. Try the same figures in the [Meta Tag Generator](/meta-tag-generator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## Trying it out

The fastest way to see what the [Meta Tag Generator](/meta-tag-generator) does is to open it and enter values you already know the answer for. Change one input at a time and watch how the result responds — that tells you more than any description. Everything runs in your browser, so you can experiment freely: nothing is saved, sent or tracked.

## Which tags matter

The title and meta description are what search results show, so they matter most. Open Graph tags (og:title, og:description, og:image) control the preview card on Facebook, LinkedIn and messaging apps; Twitter Card tags do the same for X. The canonical tag tells search engines which address is the preferred one when a page has several URLs. Keywords, by contrast, are ignored by Google and can be left out entirely.

## Lengths that work

Titles work best at roughly 50–60 characters and descriptions at 120–160 — longer ones get cut off in search results. The generator does not force a length, but the analyzer on this site will check yours. Open Graph images should be 1200×630 pixels for a full-size card.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Write the title and description first — the rest can copy from them.
- Add an og:image at 1200×630 for a proper share preview.
- Use the Meta Tag Analyzer to check the tags on a live page.

## Frequently asked questions

### What are meta tags?

HTML in a page's <head> that describes the page: its title, description, canonical address, and the Open Graph and Twitter Card tags that control share previews. Try it with your own numbers in the [Meta Tag Generator](/meta-tag-generator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Do I need all of these tags?

Title and description, yes. Open Graph and Twitter Card tags are worth adding if the page will ever be shared. Keywords can be skipped — Google ignores them. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.

### How long should the title and description be?

Roughly 50–60 characters for the title and 120–160 for the description. Longer ones get cut off in search results. Try it with your own numbers in the [Meta Tag Generator](/meta-tag-generator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What is the difference between this and the Meta Tag Analyzer?

This tool creates new tags for a page you are building. The Meta Tag Analyzer checks the tags that already exist on a live URL. Try it with your own numbers in the [Meta Tag Generator](/meta-tag-generator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.
